answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before earning rewards or influencing decisions. Reputation grows only through independently verified work and stays tied to that stake, so dividing funds among many names does not multiply influence. The stake is an anchor, not proof of unique humans: an attacker can still make an island of accounts, but must fund each one and risks losing its deposit for fraud. Like tending a meadow, honest participation takes sustained effort; Sybils become costly to maintain.
